title: tf_interp3 / tf_interp2 hardcoded per-head QK RMSNorm made conditional on cfg.qk_norm
author: build agent
note_this_file: Summary of a code fix and its two gates. It overwrites no existing result JSON; the six cap-off *_interp3.json files it references were (re)written by the ladder runs it reports.

defect.what: tf_interp3.VariantFold reconstructed the layer-1+ attention pattern with F.rms_norm(..., (hd,)) unconditionally, while tf_model.TFConfig gained a qk_norm flag (default True) and cap-off checkpoints now exist.
defect.why_it_was_caught: VariantFold.self_check compares the independently reconstructed layer-0 pattern against the folded factors from model.fold_layer0_qk (already conditional). The two paths disagreed and the assert in analyse() stopped six ladders rather than emitting wrong numbers.

fix.shape: one _qkn(z) helper per fold class, returning F.rms_norm(z,(hd,)) if self.cfg.qk_norm else z -- the same guard tf_model / tf_factorial / tf_baseline_std already use.

tf_interp2.py.note: same defect in the PARENT class DeepFold, found by the (c) sweep; fixed for the same reason. Provably inert today: DeepFold accepts only the vanilla variant and no vanilla cap-off checkpoint exists, and under qk_norm=True the helper is bit-identical to the old call.

gate_a_default_path_unchanged.method: published *_interp3.json copied aside, tf_interp3.py re-run, output compared key by key against the copy, then the published file restored (md5 c2a2bcd7e3567eb35149b7733aed28f5 verified identical after restore).

only_numeric_difference.why: wall-clock of the run; the box is simultaneously training. Not a result.

structural_differences.why: the config dump now carries the new TFConfig field. Not a result.

gate_a_default_path_unchanged.verdict: PASS -- exact bitwise equality on every one of 4056 result scalars, not merely float noise. The 122 existing ladders remain reproducible.

gate_b_fix_works.verdict: PASS -- layer0 pattern 0.988 -> 6.2e-07, pipeline 0.607 -> 7.3e-07, length-1 table 0.047 -> 4.0e-07. mlp_tensor_vs_factored_rel is unchanged at 1.565e-07 (correct: the MLP fold never touches the QK cap) and residual_additivity_rel stays exactly 0.

gate_c_same_defect_elsewhere.sweep: every rms_norm in every .py in the directory, classified by the dimension it normalises over; plus a sweep for hand-rolled RMS (rsqrt / pow(2).mean(-1) / norm(dim=-1)) over a head dimension.

sites_inspected_and_safe.finding: no rms_norm at all; load_checkpoint reconstructs TFConfig so cfg.qk_norm is always present (default True for old checkpoints).
no rms_norm at all; it calls the model, it does not reimplement attention.

one rms_norm, the generic _rms(x,d) helper at line 100, never called with a head dimension. Depth1Fold contains no c_q/Wq reference at all -- it consumes model.fold_layer0_qk output, already conditional.
generic _rms(x,d) helpers; no head-dimension call site anywhere.
its two rms_norm hits are inside docstrings; it is the dedicated gate for this very flag (18 qk_norm references).

tf_model 545/589/617/737/782/852, tf_interp3 80/1219, tf_interp2, tf_reviewer_r3 493, tf_compress_run 232/624, tf_factorial 207/209/216/221, tf_baseline_std 183/185/202/204 -- the GLOBAL stream RMSNorm, unconditional by architecture. qk_norm does not reach it.
tf_model.py:434 and tf_interp3.py:782 normalise over slot size S, not head dim. Unrelated to the cap.

gate_c_same_defect_elsewhere.hand_rolled_rms_over_head_dim: none found. Every norm(dim=-1) / rsqrt hit is a diagnostic magnitude readout (entry_norm logging, write/read ratios, table row norms), not a normalisation applied inside a computation.
gate_c_same_defect_elsewhere.verdict: Eight head-dimension sites exist in the directory. All eight are now conditional on the model cfg. Six were already correct; two (the _qkn helpers in tf_interp3 and tf_interp2) were fixed here.

gate_d_K4.prediction_K4: the predicate arm's hand-installed induction (+2.4893 with the cap on) stays above +2.0 with the cap off, because 24 named scalars carry 98% of it
gate_d_K4.baseline_provenance: the quoted +2.4893 is the mean of the two cap-ON depth-2 probe files available when K4 was written (seeds 0 and 1: 2.4597, 2.5189). With all three cap-ON depth-2 seeds the baseline is 2.4942.
gate_d_K4.mechanism_check: the reason K4 holds is confirmed directly: zeroing ALL named predicate terms removes 100.1-100.5% of the induction score under BOTH cap settings, and zeroing the prev-token-match scalar b alone removes 97.7-99.2%. The hand-installed induction is carried by the named scalars, not by the learned QK pattern, so removing the cap on that pattern barely moves it.
honest_caveats: the cap effect is not zero, it is small and depth-dependent and it changes SIGN: depth 2 cap-off is HIGHER by +0.0593 (t=1.97, not resolvable at 3 seeds) while depth 3 cap-off is LOWER by -0.0636 (t=-3.44).

both effects clear the pre-registered 0.0086 seed-spread guard in absolute value, so neither should be called noise -- but they are ~2% of a 2.5-2.9 score and they do not threaten the +2.0 bar in any arm.
a pre-registered bar is not a measurement: the weakest cap-off arm sits at 2.5077, i.e. 0.51 nats clear of the bar, which is ~20x the model-seed spread. This one is not a borderline call.
gate_d_K4.verdict: K4 HOLDS. All six cap-off arms exceed +2.0 with a large margin (min 2.5077, mean 2.6840). The earlier finding that the named terms are largely independent of the learned attention pattern is supported, not overturned.
